line: So. You are the new sawbones the Guild sent me. Kreuzer, is it?

line: Apothecary-surgeon, sworn at Weissburg. I have my letters, Master Haller—

line: Letters. Letters don’t stop a man bleeding into the straw. Hands do. Show me your hands.
context: I · Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful

line: …Steady enough. Sister! Our young doctor has arrived just in time for the Tuesday knife-fights.
context: I · Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful

line: Sister Ilse, of the Merciful Order. I keep the instruments, the ledgers, and the Master’s temper.
context: I · Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful

line: There’s a drover on the table already. Somebody at the Gilded Goose disagreed with his dice.
context: I · Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful

line: Knife wounds. Simple work. Stitch him, drain him, salve him. I’ll watch.
context: I · Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful

line: And Kreuzer — in this hospice we do not lose patients to simple work.
context: I · Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful

line: Two deep cuts. Take the gut thread and zig-zag across each wound to stitch it.
Cross the wound again and again, moving along it. One smooth stroke earns the best marks.
Blood’s pooling. Hold the leech-pipe over it to draw it off.
You can’t stitch through a pool of blood — drain first.
Just nicks left. Brush Saint’s Salve over the small ones — no need for thread.
Make way! Make way, damn you! Surgeon! Where’s the surgeon?
context: I · The Hospice — the next morning

line: Captain Mauer of the Watch. Lower your voice, Captain, this is a house of mercy.
context: I · The Hospice — the next morning

line: Horned raiders hit the timber-road caravan at dawn. We drove them off, but young Pieter took a shaft in the side.
context: I · The Hospice — the next morning

line: Beast-folk fletch their arrows with barbed heads. Rip one straight out and you’ll tear half his side with it.
context: I · The Hospice — the next morning

line: Nick the flesh at the entry with the lancet — twice — to free the barbs. Then pull. Cleanly.

line: The arrow’s barbed. Lancet first — two nicks at the entry wound. Then seize it with the tongs and pull it well clear.
Then drain and stitch the wound it leaves.
The bolt in his thigh has no barbs. Tongs, and pull it straight out.
Quick, clean pulls earn the best marks.
Doctor, the gunsmiths’ quarter. An apprentice was proving a new handgun barrel and it burst in his hands.
Burns across the chest and lead fragments driven under the skin.
Powder burns. The charred skin is dead — pluck the eschar away with tongs before you salve, or it festers.
The shot is in deep. You’ll have to open him. Trace the line I’ve inked, and keep your hand true.
He’s lost blood already. If his pulse flags, the tincture — hold it to the flesh and let it take.
His pulse is weak already. Hold the tincture to the flesh to steady him if you need it.
Burns first. Pluck the black eschar away with the tongs, then salve the raw flesh.
Now open him along the inked line with the lancet. Keep to the line — start at the glowing end.
There — the shot. Pull each ball out with the tongs.
Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the thread.
Doctor… this one was found in the Tanners’ Rows. Swellings at the neck and groin. Fever. Maggots in a sore.
Buboes. Lance them before they burst, draw off the pus, and salve the wound. Rot-patches creep back if you dawdle.
And the grubs — the cautery brand. Hold it on them until they stop wriggling. Mind you don’t sear good flesh.
A plague case. In the city. How very interesting.
…Inquisitor Stroh. Of the Ash Tribunal.
Please, do carry on, Doctor. I only wish to watch. Pestilence so often has a sponsor.
Lance each bubo with a single touch of the lancet before it bursts. Then drain the pus and salve it.
Grubs in the sore! The cautery brand — hold it on each one until it stops moving.
Don’t linger on bare flesh with the brand.
The rot’s spreading. Salve every patch — quickly, it creeps back.
The choir… they’re singing in me… make them stop singing…
context: I · The Hospice — the small hours

line: Doctor, look at his chest. Those marks — they’re moving.
context: I · The Hospice — the small hours

line: …That is no disease. Those are sigils. Someone has written on this boy.
context: I · The Hospice — the small hours

line: Kreuzer. Listen to me carefully. Sear the sigils out with the brand — trace every stroke.
context: I · The Hospice — the small hours

line: And if something… answers… when you do — there is an old apothecary’s rite. The Litany of Stillness.
context: I · The Hospice — the small hours

line: Trace the five-pointed star and still your heart. For a few breaths, the world will wait for you.
context: I · The Hospice — the small hours

line: Do not do it where the Inquisitor can see. The Tribunal does not distinguish between a prayer and a spell.
context: I · The Hospice — the small hours

line: Those sigils are draining him. Trace every stroke of each one with the brand to sear it out.
Something is moving beneath the skin. We have to open him. The lancet — along the line.
Saints preserve us… what is that?
Doctor — if ever there were a time for the Litany, it is now. Draw the star with the right hand.
It’s gone. Tend the wounds it left.
Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the thread.
Doctor… after it broke, a word was left seared into the flesh. Matins.
The first of the canonical hours. The first prayer of the night.
A curse that lives and fights like a beast, and signs itself like a psalm. A Malison.
And if this was Matins… then somewhere, someone is already writing Lauds.
A remarkable recovery, Doctor. Remarkable.
Tell me — at the end, your hands moved so very quickly. Almost as if time itself were… obliging you.
Practice, Inquisitor. And the grace of Saint Ildra.
Of course. The grace of the Saint. I shall pray on it.
Don’t look at me like that, Doctor. I didn’t ask for you. The Inquisitor “suggested” it to the Burgomaster.

line: So he can watch you somewhere with fewer witnesses.
context: II · The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf

line: We’re clearing the Grauwald of raiders before the spring caravans. My lads need a surgeon more than a city needs rumours.
context: II · The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf

line: Speaking of which — the scouts came back. Two of them. Something followed them out of the barrow-fields.
context: II · The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf

line: Doctor, it’s a gravehound bite. Claw rakes across the back, and — look — it left its teeth in him.
context: II · The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf

line: Corpse-eaters carry a venom in their spit. Hold the tincture to the bite itself and it will draw the poison.
context: II · The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf

line: The venom first — hold the tincture on the bite until it takes.
The longer it spreads, the harder it drags on him.
Now the fangs. Tongs — pull each one clear.
Claw rakes. Three deep lines — drain and stitch each.
Put me down, you long-legged oafs! I can walk! I can… mostly walk.
Dwarf prospector. Her crew was working a seam in the hills when it caved in.
The rock went black, Doctor. Black and wrong, like a bruise in the stone. It sang when we struck it. Then it burst.
There are shards under her skin that I can’t see — but the flesh around them is spoiling.
Master Haller sent this with me. His old Scrying Lens. Pass it slowly over the flesh and it shows what hides beneath.
Dwarf hide’s thicker than yours, lad. You’ll want a strong arm on that thread.
Rock splinters on the surface first. Tongs.
Now — the Scrying Lens. Pass it slowly over the flesh; where something hides, it shimmers.
Hold it still over the shimmer to bring the shard to light, then pull it.
Clean up the spoiled flesh and any wounds left.
Forager. Went to check his snares near the old web-trees. We found him wrapped up like a Martinmas ham.
A web-spinner bite. Venom, spreading fast. And these lumps under the skin… Saints. She laid in him.
Lance the sacs before they hatch, Doctor, and sear what spills out. If they hatch on their own, they’ll scatter.
Venom from two bites. Tincture on each, quickly.
The sacs — lance each one with a single touch, then sear the hatchlings with the brand.
Mind the ones that are close to hatching.
One more sac, deeper. Use the lens to find it, then open it.
And he’s taken a fever-bubo from the bite — lance and cleanse it.
Doctor. I have brought you a gift.
context: II · The muster camp — before midnight

line: A lay-cantor of the Hollow Choir. We took him in the barrow-fields, singing to the dead.
context: II · The muster camp — before midnight

line: The moment he began to confess, those marks ignited. His masters would rather he burned than spoke.
context: II · The muster camp — before midnight

line: He also swallowed something. You will keep him alive. I have questions, and the dead are poor at answering them.
context: II · The muster camp — before midnight

line: …Doctor. Whatever he is, he’s a patient.
context: II · The muster camp — before midnight

line: On the table. Now.

line: The poison he swallowed — tincture, now, or he’s gone before we start.
Those sigils are burning him from within. Sear each one out — every stroke.
The hexfire burns. Pluck the eschar, then salve them.
Maggots in an old sore — the Tribunal’s cells are filthy. Brand them.
Lauds… is sung at dawn… with the muster… under the banner…
The dawn muster? That’s now — the whole company’s singing the morning hymn—
Doctor! It’s Jorg, the standard-bearer — his chest is moving… it’s singing back!
Clear a table. Sister — every instrument we have.
We have to open him — along the line, Doctor.
Saints… it has a choir. Those little lights are its Voices — hold the brand on each as it circles.
Silence all of them and its heart will be bare.
It’s done. Tend what it left of him.
Close him up. Gently — he has a banner to carry.
Two of them now. Matins in the city, Lauds in my own camp. Someone is keeping time, Doctor.
Six more hours to the full Office. Prime. Terce. Sext. None. Vespers. Compline.
Doctor Kreuzer.
When that thing screamed, every candle in this tent stopped flickering. The flames stood still. For eight heartbeats.
I counted.
…The morning air is very still, Inquisitor.
So it is. We will speak at length, you and I. After Prime.
Too much blood — draw it off with the leech-pipe before you stitch!
The hexstone is corrupting the flesh around it — get it out!
Barbed! Nick the flesh at the entry with the lancet before you pull.
The dead flesh is off. Now salve the raw burn.
Pluck away the charred eschar with the tongs first!
Draw off the pus before you salve it.
The choir is silenced — its heart is bare! Brand it, now!
It’s calling its Voices back!
It’s singing — every verse tears him open! Stitch the cuts as they come!
There! It’s surfacing — finish it!
The Voices shield it. Silence them first — hold the brand on each as it circles.
It’s gone under the skin! The Scrying Lens — hunt it down!
It shattered — hexstone, everywhere! Get every shard out before it spoils him!
That sac is moving… it’s about to hatch!
Spiderlings! Brand them before they scatter!
Its shroud has parted — sear it with the brand, now!
It’s tearing the flesh as it moves! Stitch those wounds!
The brand can’t touch it while it’s veiled. Wait for the shroud to part!
It’s shedding hexlings! Burn them before they feed!
It’s splitting apart! Seize every shard with the tongs and cast it out — before they rejoin!
Careful! The brand is searing healthy flesh!
Vitals are failing! Use the tincture, Doctor!
The operation is complete.
Instruments ready, Doctor.
